subject: PulseHealth: sudden p95 latency increase - Model Omega v3
messages:
From: Andrew Ballard <andrew.ballard@pulsehealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@pulsehealth.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in response latency affecting PulseHealth triage (Model Omega v3)

Hi Monica,

We're seeing a sharp increase in end-to-end NLP latency for our triage flow starting ~07:55 PT. p95 has jumped from ~420ms to ~1.6s in the past 20 minutes and user complaints are coming in. This map to requests routed to Model Omega v3 (variant: quant-8).

Quick data:
- Impacted routes: /triage/v1/complete, /triage/v1/priority
- Observed p50/p95: 260ms / 1600ms (target p95 450ms)
- Error rate: no increase observed, just high tail latency

I've attached a short span export and a few sample traces for your infra team to look at. We can share access to our internal Grafana if it's useful.

Attachments: [p95_trace.zip (csv + spans)]

Can you confirm whether anything changed on your side (rollout, kernel, quant variant)? If this is a known degradation, we need fallback/rollback guidance and an ETA.

Thanks,
Andrew
Director, Platform Ops
PulseHealth

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Andrew Ballard <andrew.ballard@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 08:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in response latency affecting PulseHealth triage (Model Omega v3)

Andrew — thanks for the quick heads-up and the trace. We see the same from our telemetry. I'm looping in Karthik (serving runtime) and Markus (SRE/rollouts).

Plan for the next 90 minutes:
- Karthik to triage kernel/quantization path and determine whether v3 introduced a perf regression.
- If we confirm regression, we'll propose either a targeted fallback (route PulseHealth to Omega v2) or a rollback of the v3 variant.
- I'll prepare a provisional SLA exception request in case we need to switch traffic immediately.

Could you grant engineering temporary read access to the PulseHealth request traces and the API key used in the 07:45–08:10 window? That'll speed up root-cause.

—Monica
Senior Customer Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Andrew Ballard <andrew.ballard@pulsehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in response latency affecting PulseHealth triage (Model Omega v3)

Adding initial triage notes — attaching a short engine trace.

Findings (quick):
- The degradation aligns with a kernel dispatch change introduced in Omega v3 (commit d4c9f8) that affects fused attention paths for sequence lengths ~128–256. PulseHealth workload has a tight length distribution in that band.
- Quant-8 variant shows higher variance post-change; CPU fallback path triggers under moderate concurrency and causes tail amplification.
- No increase in 5xx errors; requests are completing but with longer queueing in the runtime.

Options:
1) Immediate traffic redirect for PulseHealth to Omega v2 (non-quantized) — minimal data risk, expected p95 restoration to baseline within minutes.
2) Emergency rollback of Omega v3 variant across the cluster — larger blast radius, requires release manager sign-off and post-rollback verification.
3) Apply a temporary routing policy (circuit-breaker) to route only PulseHealth's keys off the quantized variant to a compatible v3 non-quantized build — requires quick build & deploy (~1–2 hours).

I'm recommending option 1 for fastest mitigation while we validate a permanent fix. If we proceed with option 1, SRE can enact traffic pin at the routing layer and monitor p95 for the next 30m.

Attachment: [engine_trace_omega_v3.log]

Karthik
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: REQUEST: provisional SLA carveout & approval to pin PulseHealth to Omega v2 (fast mitigation)

Evelyn —

PulseHealth (deal HUB-38291) is experiencing a rapid p95 tail spike attributable to Omega v3's recent kernel change (Karthik's short triage below). Customer impact: production triage latency rising to ~1.6s p95; they are reporting user-visible slowdowns.

Proposal (recommended):
- Approve a provisional SLA carveout for PulseHealth while we execute an immediate routing pin so their traffic is served by Omega v2 (expected p95 rollback to baseline). The carveout is to acknowledge that impacted requests may exceed contractual p95 temporarily during the mitigation window.
- Authorization to perform a targeted routing pin (option 1 from Karthik) within the next 30 minutes. SRE will monitor and provide a rollback/restore runbook.

Impact/constraints:
- Revenue risk: PulseHealth is a mid-enterprise account with weekly usage committed; ongoing slowdowns increase churn risk.
- Duration: provisional carveout request is for up to 8 hours while we validate a permanent fix and schedule a controlled rollout of a corrected v3.

Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/38291, internal dashboard: https://app.redwood-inference.internal/dashboards/pulsehealth?range=1h
Attachments: [rollback_runbook.md]

Please approve or advise an alternate mitigation.

Thanks,
Monica

Please proceed and confirm when traffic is pinned.

—Evelyn

Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 10:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in response latency affecting PulseHealth triage (Model Omega v3)

Andrew — quick update and mitigation timeline.

Per leadership authorization, we will pin PulseHealth traffic to Omega v2 at 10:30 PT. Actions scheduled:
- 10:20 PT: SRE will snapshot routing tables and compose a rollback ticket.
- 10:30 PT: Execute routing pin for PulseHealth API keys (expected cutover <2 minutes).
- 10:35–11:05 PT: Intensified monitoring for p50/p95 and error rates; alert thresholds will be lowered for the customer-facing routes.
- Post-rollback: we'll share the runbook and a short post-mortem within 4 hours.

We expect p95 to return to baseline with option 1. If not, we'll escalate for a full rollback and coordinate a customer-facing timeline.

Thanks for the patience — we'll confirm when the pin is active.

Markus Klein
Production SRE Lead
Redwood Inference
